title: Chicken or Turkey with Stuffing and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of roasted chicken or turkey breast stuffed with a blend of whole grains, herbs and spices, accompanied by a side of carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale or Swiss chard). It is prepared without sauce, preserving the natural flavors of the meat and vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed protein sources worldwide.
Stuffings often include whole grains such as quinoa or buckwheat, adding extra satiety.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C and compounds that support the body’s detox pathways.
Dark‑green leafy greens provide high amounts of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
The absence of sauce reduces added sugars and sodium.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply a complete set of essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Bone health support
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens are excellent sources of calcium, magnesium and vitamin K, contributing to strong bones.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leaves contain carotenoids and flavonoids that combat free radicals.

items.title: Low added sugar and sodium
items.content: Without sauce, the dish allows better control of salt and sugar intake, benefiting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive roasting can make the meat dry, which may affect digestion.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked poultry can harbor Salmonella; ensure an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: Certain greens (e.g., spinach) are high in oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the meat into portions and arranging the vegetables on the plate. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice or a drizzle of herb‑infused olive oil can be added for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
